Lessons.Title: Problems About Perimeter and Area
ExplanationParagraphs: Source 2021 goal: convert measures with multiplication/division and solve multi-step area and perimeter problems, preserving units and teacher-observed geometric models.

Warm-up: shaded rectilinear grid; Activity 1: 36-in × 24-in poster cut to an 8-in-high, 8-ft-long banner; Activity 2: a six-sided classroom measured in inches, yards and feet. Teacher checks original diagrams.
Banner: 36×24=864 in². Eight feet=96 inches, so 8×96=768 in²; 96 square inches spare. Cutting three 36×8-in strips and trimming 12×8 inches can actually make a 96×8-in banner.
Classroom sides: bottom 204in=17ft, right 4yd=12ft, inset left 3yd=9ft, inset rise 3ft, top 8ft and left 180in=15ft.
Perimeter=17+12+9+3+8+15=64ft=768in; the 1200-inch delivery is enough with 432 inches spare. Area=(17×12)+(8×3)=228ft².
First-party Cool-down (not the gated publisher item): a 12ft by 8ft room has area 96ft² and perimeter 40ft. Student drawing and physical cutting remain teacher reviewed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Convert all linear units first
KeyConcepts.Definition: Twelve inches make one foot; three feet make one yard.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use matching units before addition or area multiplication.

KeyConcepts.Title: Area conserved by cutting and rearranging
KeyConcepts.Definition: A cut-and-rejoined rectangle can preserve the amount of paper.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare square inches AND demonstrate a feasible arrangement.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rectilinear perimeter and floor area
KeyConcepts.Definition: Perimeter adds outside linear lengths; area adds non-overlapping rectangles.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use all six sides for perimeter and partition the L-shaped floor.

WorkedExamples.Title: Banner measurement and a feasible cut
WorkedExamples.Question: Is a 36in-by-24in sheet enough for a banner 8in high and 8ft long?
WorkedExamples.Method: Convert to inches, compare area and show construction.
Steps: 864−768=96in² left. Cut three 36×8 strips, join to 108×8 and trim 12×8.

WorkedExamples.Title: Poster paper area
WorkedExamples.Question: What is the area of the original 36in-by-24in paper?

WorkedExamples.Title: Six-sided classroom baseboard length
WorkedExamples.Question: Classroom sides 204in, 4yd, 3yd, 3ft, 8ft, 180in: how many feet and inches of baseboard?
WorkedExamples.Method: Convert first, then add all six outside lengths.
WorkedExamples.Check: Every outside side is included exactly once.

WorkedExamples.Title: Check baseboard delivery
WorkedExamples.Question: A delivery has 1200in of baseboard. Is it enough for a perimeter of 768in?
WorkedExamples.Method: Subtract required length from supplied length.

WorkedExamples.Title: Carpet for the L-shaped floor
WorkedExamples.Question: The floor is a 17ft-by-12ft base plus an 8ft-by-3ft upper extension. How much carpet?

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent Edulytics Cool-down
WorkedExamples.Question: Find the area and perimeter of a 12ft by 8ft rectangular room.
WorkedExamples.Method: Area is product; perimeter is twice the sum.
WorkedExamples.Check: Keep squared and linear units distinct.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat 8 feet of banner length as 8 inches.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A foot has twelve inches; the required banner length is 96in.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Add yard, foot and inch numbers without conversion.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The numerical sum cannot represent a consistent perimeter.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Convert all six sides to feet: 17+12+9+3+8+15=64ft.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use a full 17-by-15 rectangle for the L-shaped room.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The absent 9ft-by-3ft corner would be counted as carpet.

SummaryPoints: Room baseboard is 64ft=768in, so 1200in delivery leaves 432in.
L-shaped carpet area is 228ft², using non-overlapping rectangles.
Teacher reviews source figures, inch tiles and construction; Cool-down is independent.
